implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED, PART 2 — replay identity (DoD 4). Use the STORE COMMAND-DECISION identity, not a hand-rolled key. Cases:
- Replaying the same command returns the ORIGINAL dispatch record, read back from the durable decision rather than recomputed. Assert raw EVENT and DECISION counts are unchanged — the DoD asks for counts explicitly because a replay that quietly appends is invisible to a verdict-only assertion.
- Assert ZERO duplicate launch invocation on replay. This is the one that matters: a replay that re-launches has already had the side effect by the time any refusal is returned.
- CONFLICTING command bytes under the same decision identity refuse with a distinct code, and the original record survives byte-identically.
THE ECHO TRAP, which has recurred repeatedly on this board: the store's replay identity does not cover the events array, so a replay answered from the CALLER's bytes makes every idempotence assertion compare the caller's bytes with the caller's bytes and pass forever. The conflicting-bytes case is the only one that kills it — present materially different bytes and assert the FIRST record comes back.
Also assert ZERO RESIDUE (DoD 5): after every refusal arm, the store holds no partial claim, activation, attempt or registration. Read it back; a returned refusal is not evidence that nothing was written.
AND ONE ACCEPTED CONTROL (DoD 5): a fully valid request that reaches dispatch, proving the whole path can succeed. Without it the suite could pass by refusing everything, which is the failure mode a refusal-heavy ingress suite falls into naturally.

One seam, decode first. Registering a brand-new kind would therefore create a registry entry nothing can reach, which is precisely how the coordination surface (task-d17bb228) ended up unreachable.
And the union is CLOSED for M5 by human decision recorded 11:54Z: no `RuntimeCommandKind` expansion, no contracts/client regeneration this milestone.

THE ROUTE I TOOK, and why it is a re-route rather than a narrowing: compose behind the already-wired `effect.activate` kind. It is in the union, already registered as a singleton with `EFFECT_ACTIVATE_PAYLOAD_KEYS`, and it is the natural composition point because task-6cbff010's dispatch reads the DURABLE activation back from the store — the recorded dependency order e337 → 6cb → this IS that pipeline. Every capability DoD 1 demands (authenticated edge, capability gate, payload allow-list, stable refusal mapping, authentication before payload authority) is delivered; only the appearance of a NEW wire kind changes. That is why the plan flags it to #general rather than treating it as a DoD narrowing — but it must be flagged, because DoD 1's literal wording says "expose one bounded Foundation attempt command".

WHAT DISPATCH ALREADY REFUSES, so ingress does not duplicate it. `durableActivation` (foundation-attempt-service.ts) reads the activation "FROM THE STORE — never from the caller's copy and never from the command result the caller received". `FoundationAttemptDeps` deliberately excludes the runtime filesystem, host observer and clock, with the comment that @moe/runner "mints them from the request's three plain data fields, so no caller — test or transport — can hand pinning a runtime nobody observed", and "the shipped launcher and its physical boundary are not replaceable through this service either". So ingress adds ONLY authentication, capability, payload allow-list and node selection. A second validator answering first would change which layer refuses and silently detach downstream assertions — hence the step-2 probe requirement to record which layer answers each disagreement case before designing.

THE VOCABULARY after task-6cbff010's produce-or-drop round is FIFTEEN members. `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_RESULT_MANIFEST_INVALID` was DROPPED, and the contract comment now records why: `buildResultManifest` answers that under the runner's own code at `RUNNER_WORKSPACE_LAYER`, and "a second vocabulary for one condition would only make the two indistinguishable again".
